audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) The audio begins with a male voice speaking clearly with a professional tone. There is no background music initially, creating a sterile studio environment. The speech rate is moderate with natural pauses. (2) A subtle acoustic guitar plucking track fades in as the second male speaker starts talking. His voice has a noticeable accent and high pitch variability. A playful 'pop' sound effect occurs as graphic elements appear on screen. (3) The speaker's arousal increases as he imitates a parent, using a louder, more aggressive tone. A 'fire crackling' sound effect is introduced to emphasize the intensity of the parents' behavior. The guitar music remains steady in the background. (4) The tone shifts back to a calm, analytical narrative style. The BGM tempo remains consistent at around 95 BPM. Small digital UI 'ding' sound effects punctuate the explanation of the 'vicious cycle' of education. (5) The dialogue continues as a back-and-forth exchange between the two speakers. The acoustic guitar provides a rhythmic bed underneath the speech, which is well-mastered with a high signal-to-noise ratio. (6) A sharp 'whoosh' transition sound effect marks the shift to a concluding statement. The speaker maintains an authoritative yet friendly tone. The music swells slightly in volume toward the very end before fading out during the call to action.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video aims to critique the 'cram school' culture and systemic issues in Taiwanese English education through an interview with a foreign teacher. It highlights how parental pressure and a curriculum focused on memorization rather than practice create a cycle where students are afraid to speak the language.
